Mixing (2) and (4) results in the same red precipitate, and gas bubbles are observed. When mixing (3) and (5) a white precipitate is formed. However, when an excess of (5) is added to (3) the precipitate dissolves. Mixing (3) and (6) results in a white precipitate. Mixing (4) and (5) also results in a white precipitate. When (6) is added to the mixture of (4) and (5) the precipitate dissolves and gas bubbles can be observed. When mixing (4) and (6) the solution gets cloudy and gas bubbles can be observed.
